I am submitting this complaint because a collection account that was previously removed from my credit reports after my prior CFPB complaint has now been reported again by a different collection agency. 

I have documentation showing that the previous collection agency removed the account following the resolution of my earlier CFPB complaint. Despite that resolution, another collection agency has now purchased or been assigned the same alleged debt and began reporting it on my credit reports again. 

I dispute the accuracy, completeness, and legal basis for this reporting.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) requires furnishers of information to provide accurate information to consumer reporting agencies. 
15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) requires furnishers to conduct a reasonable investigation after receiving notice of a dispute from a consumer reporting agency.

15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) requires consumer reporting agencies to follow reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy of information contained in consumer reports.

15 U.S.C. 1681i requires consumer reporting agencies to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of disputed information.

Additionally, under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) : 15 U.S.C. 1692e prohibits debt collectors from using any false, deceptive, or misleading representations in connection with the collection of a debt.

15 U.S.C. 1692f prohibits unfair or unconscionable means to collect or attempt to collect a debt.

If applicable, 15 U.S.C. 1692g requires the debt collector to provide validation of the debt when required by law.

Because this account was previously removed following my CFPB complaint, I request that the current collection agency provide competent evidence demonstrating : Their legal authority to collect the alleged debt. 
A complete chain of assignment or ownership from the original creditor to the current collector. 
Documentation establishing the amount claimed is accurate. 
Documentation demonstrating that their credit reporting complies with the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Fair Debt Collection Practices Act. 
If they can not provide competent evidence supporting the accuracy and legal basis for this reporting, I request that the account be immediately deleted from all consumer reporting agencies. 
I am attaching documentation showing : The previous CFPB complaint. 
The resolution of that complaint. 
Evidence that the prior collection account was removed. 
Documentation showing the new collection account has now appeared.

The conflicting information regarding how the payment would be applied was disclosed only during a telephone conversation immediately before payment was to be made.

I am prepared to provide all supporting documentation and correspondence upon request.

BACKGROUND AND CHRONOLOGY OF EVENTS On or about XX/XX/year>, I received an email communication from Resurgent Capital Services, XXXX ( Resurgent ) regarding an alleged debt. 

Immediately upon receiving this communication, I submitted a written dispute and request for validation of the alleged debt pursuant to the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), 15 U.S.C. 1692g. In my dispute, I requested documentation sufficient to establish the existence, amount, ownership, and collectability of the alleged debt, including documentation demonstrating Resurgents authority to collect and a complete accounting of the balance claimed.

Rather than providing meaningful verification, XXXX responded by sending account statements that merely repeated information already in their possession. The documents provided identified XXXX XXXX as the creditor but failed to identify either Resurgent Capital Services, L.P. or LVNV Funding LLC as the legal owner of the alleged debt. The documents also failed to establish any chain of assignment, transfer, or sale demonstrating how ownership of the alleged debt passed from XXXX XXXX to LVNV Funding LLC or how Resurgent obtained authority to collect on XXXX behalf. 

As a result, the materials provided failed to establish that XXXX or LVNV possesses a legal interest in the alleged debt or has standing to collect it. The documents did not address the substantive issues raised in my dispute and failed to provide evidence sufficient to establish that the debt is valid, accurately calculated, legally collectible, or owned by the entities attempting to collect it. 

XXXX. SPECIFIC LEGAL VIOLATIONS A. Failure to Provide XXXX XXXX of the Alleged Debt. 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) After receiving my timely dispute, Resurgent was required to cease collection efforts until it obtained and mailed verification of the debt.

The materials provided by Resurgent consisted primarily of account statements and failed to provide documentation establishing : The basis for the amount allegedly owed ; Documentation demonstrating Resurgents ownership of, or authority to collect, the alleged debt ; Documentation demonstrating that LVNV Funding LLC owns the alleged debt ; A chain of title, assignment, or transfer from XXXX XXXX to LVNV Funding LLC ; Information sufficient to verify the accuracy of the balance claimed ; Documentation addressing the specific disputes and requests raised in my validation request.

Without documentation establishing ownership and authority to collect, the materials provided fail to demonstrate that either entity has standing to pursue collection of the alleged debt. 

By merely providing account statements that repeated the amount claimed without adequately responding to the issues raised in my dispute, XXXX failed to provide meaningful verification of the alleged debt. 

B. Continued Collection Activity Following an Inadequate Response. 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) Despite receiving my dispute, XXXX treated its limited response as sufficient verification and continued efforts to collect the alleged debt. C. Such conduct constitutes a false, deceptive, or misleading representation in connection with the collection of a debt in violation of 15 U.S.C. 1692e.

D. Unfair Collection Practices. 15 U.S.C. 1692f Attempting to collect a disputed debt without providing documentation reasonably sufficient to verify the debt, establish ownership, demonstrate authority to collect, and address the consumers dispute constitutes an unfair and unconscionable collection practice.

I did not apply for this account, did not authorize anyone to apply for it on my behalf, and never received or used the card. The charges on this account, totaling approximately {$31000.00}, are the result of identity theft. 

I discovered the fraudulent account in approximately XX/XX/XXXX. Upon discovering it, I filed an Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission on XX/XX/XXXX ; my FTC report number is XXXX.

In response to that complaint, XXXX XXXX acknowledged in writing that the account was opened through an online application and that no signed application exists. XXXX XXXX stated it concluded the account belongs to me based on two facts : ( 1 ) a phone number that XXXX XXXX says it confirmed belongs to me was used to activate the account, and ( XXXX ) a payment was made from a XXXX  XXXX deposit account that XXXX XXXX says links to me.

XXXX XXXX has not explained how it " confirmed '' the number belongs to me, and I believe its confirmation rests on its own internal records of the fraudulent application meaning XXXX XXXX is treating the phone number the identity thief provided as proof that the account is mine. Second, the XXXX XXXX deposit account that XXXX XXXX says " links to '' me is also not mine. I do not have, and have never opened, any deposit account with XXXX XXXX. XXXX XXXX 's response was the first time I was informed of this deposit account 's existence. A fraud account manager at XXXX XXXX confirmed to me by phone that no further documentation would be provided.

California Financial Code  22303 caps interest rates on consumer installment loans under $XXXX at 36% APR. The 179.00% APR reflected in the alleged loan agreement is nearly five times this statutory cap. California Financial Code  22651 renders loans made in violation of this cap void  meaning no person has the right to collect principal, charges, or recompense on the loan.

On XXXX XXXX XXXX  one week after the alleged loan was purportedly originated  the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX) entered a Settlement Agreement against CreditNinja Lending, LLC (California Finance Lender License No. XXXX), citing violations of California Financial Code Sections 22303, 22304, 22304.5, 22305, and 22320.5  the exact provisions governing the rate cap applicable to this alleged obligation. I am filing this complaint because a law firm that collects XXXX assessments has created and is attempting to collect an inflated, largely feedriven debt on my home through misleading and unfair practices. 

I am a homeowner at XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX subdivision in XXXX, Missouri. My XXXX uses XXXX XXXX XXXX as its XXXX XXXX XXXX and The Rickel Law Firm , P.C . as its thirdparty collection attorney. Rickel identifies itself in writing as a debt collector and advertises XXXX collection services that often come at no cost or no upfront cost to the association because the delinquent owner is charged the fees. Rickel has also been added as power of attorney ( POA ) for the XXXX on my account, and it filed a lien against my property electronically in that role. 

In XXXX I was sued over XXXX assessments. I was out of town and only learned of the lawsuit a few days before the scheduled hearing. I later discovered that important papers had been sent to an old address, so I was not properly notified in time, was not fully prepared for court, and did not understand the case. At that point, I was told by the attorney that I needed to sign a consent judgment in order to avoid going to court and to save my home. I was never given a proper, detailed, itemized invoice or a full ledger before signing. I was not told that I could dispute the underlying amounts, request validation of the debt, or challenge the collection and attorney fees. I signed under pressure to avoid losing my home, without understanding the full breakdown of charges and without having a fair chance to respond to the lawsuit. 

Afterward, I paid thousands of dollars under that consent judgment, including an additional large payment to stop a sheriffs levy. Despite these payments, the alleged balance on my account has continued to grow. 

In addition to the lawsuits and consent judgment, Rickel Law Firm, acting as POA for the XXXX, recorded a lien against my property for more than {$7000.00} for assessments only, and the lien document specifically states that this amount is exclusive of attorney fees and collection costs. That lien was filed electronically by Rickel Law Firm, but it does not have any ledger or detailed account history attached, so I can not verify which assessments were included, which periods they cover, or how that XXXX amount was calculated. Despite this, Rickel has demanded and attempted to collect large additional attorney and collection fees on top of that assessments only lien amount, treating the lien as if it secures a much larger, feeinflated debt that includes charges the lien itself says are not included. 

The only ledger that I have was provided by email XXXX of XXXX and it show a significant portion of what Rickel was trying to collect consisted of repeated collection, administration, flatfee, estimated localcounsel, and other lawfirm charges, not just regular HOA assessments. Many of these charges were not clearly tied to any actual work performed or to any specific authority in the XXXX governing documents. To this day, I still have not been provided with a complete, accurate XXXXside ledger from the XXXX or XXXX XXXX XXXX that would let me verify exactly which assessments, fees, and charges make up the balance Rickel is trying to collect. 

The HOAs own Paying Annual Assessments page states that homeowner assessments are billed yearly by late XXXX, due by XX/XX/XXXX, and only become delinquent after XX/XX/XXXX, and it tells homeowners to contact XXXX XXXX XXXX for assistance with their accounts. In my case, I did not receive the regular annual billing, updated ledgers, or clear account statements described there. Instead, assessments appear to have been added to an internal ledger and later treated as delinquent, with XXXX then adding its own fees and costs on top. When I contacted XXXX XXXX XXXX to request statements and a full account history, they refused to provide a complete ledger and directed me back to the law firm, leaving me without a transparent accounting of what is actually owed. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I personally appeared in court on the current XXXX XXXX lawsuit. The associations attorney from Rickel Law Firm was not prepared to proceed and asked the court to continue the case to XX/XX/XXXX, which strongly suggested they had expected to obtain a default judgment because they did not expect me to appear. While I was in the courtroom, I watched this same attorney tell another homeowner that they could sign a consent judgment in order to get a payment plan and resolve their XXXX fXXXX issue. This confirmed for me that consent judgments are being used as a routine collection tool, with homeowners pressured to sign quickly under threat of foreclosure, rather than being given a real chance to review and dispute the charges. 

I believe this conduct violates the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), including the prohibition on collecting any amount ( interest, fees, charges, or expenses ) unless that amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law. In my case, the law firm is demanding payment of large, recurring collection and attorney fees on top of a lien that is explicitly for assessments only and does not include those fees, and these charges go beyond what the XXXX governing documents clearly allow. The lack of proper notice, regular billing, and a complete ledger, along with the pressure used to obtain a consent judgment, have prevented me from understanding and disputing the debt in a fair and timely manner. 

I am asking the CFPB to review The Rickel Law Firms collection practices, including its role as POA filing electronic liens, its no cost to the association model, the way it adds and labels its fees, its use of consent judgments in XXXX XXXX cases, and XXXX XXXX XXXX role in withholding clear account statements while steering me back to the law firm. I want the inflated and unauthorized charges removed, my account corrected to reflect only lawful assessments and properly authorized charges, and for these practices to be investigated so other homeowners are not subjected to similar harm.

Here is the account information : Creditor : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Account Number : XXXX Account Type : Deposit account Date Opened : XX/XX/XXXX Date of Charge-Off : XX/XX/XXXX Balance Reported : {$4200.00} Status on my report : Account charged off, {$4200.00} written off, listed as {$4200.00} past due as of XX/XX/XXXX I have two main problems with how this account is being reported, and I want to explain both of them. 

Problem 1 The balance has not changed even though the account was charged off over 3 years ago This account was charged off in XX/XX/XXXX. That means XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX wrote off this debt more than three years ago. But my credit report still shows the exact same balance of {$4200.00} with no change at all. That does not make sense because once an account is charged off, the creditor is supposed to update how they report the balance. They can not just leave the same number sitting there forever as if nothing happened. 

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, specifically 15 U.S.C. Section 1681s-2 ( b ), companies that report information to credit bureaus are required to make sure that information is accurate and up to date. When an account is charged off, the creditor takes a tax write-off on that amount. After that happens, continuing to report the same unchanged balance as if it is still growing or still owed in the same way is misleading. I am asking Experian and the CFPB to require XXXX to either update this balance to reflect what is accurate today, or to remove the account entirely. 

Problem 2 The report says the account is still 'past due as of XX/XX/XXXX ' but it was charged off in XX/XX/XXXX My Experian report shows this account as " {$4200.00} past due as of XX/XX/XXXX. ' That language makes it look like this account just became past due recently, but that is not what happened. This account charged off back in XX/XX/XXXX, which is over three years ago. The 'past due as of " date should reflect when the account actually went delinquent, not keep updating every single month to make it look like something new is happening. 

This is a known problem with how some creditors report charged-off accounts. When a creditor keeps refreshing the 'past due as of " date on an old charge-off, it makes the negative item look much more recent than it actually is. That is unfair and inaccurate because it makes my credit report look worse than the real situation. The FCRA, under Section 1681s-2 ( b ), requires that furnishers report accurate information. Saying an account that charged off in XXXX is 'past due as of XX/XX/XXXX ' is misleading and inaccurate, and it needs to be corrected. 

Also, my report shows this account with charge-off codes ( 'CO ' ) all the way from early XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX every single month for over three years. There is no explanation of why the status and the past-due date keep getting updated on a closed, written-off account. Under FCRA Section 1681c, most negative items can only stay on a credit report for seven years from the date of first delinquency. Updating the reported date could also affect when this account is supposed to come off my report, which would be another violation. 

What I am asking for : I am asking the CFPB to look into how XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is reporting this account, and I am asking Experian to investigate it under their obligations in the FCRA. Specifically I want : Experian to investigate this account under FCRA Section 1681i and contact FirstLight to verify whether the balance and past-due date are being reported accurately ; The 'past due as of XX/XX/XXXX ' language to be corrected to reflect the actual date this account first went delinquent not a continuously refreshed current date ; The balance to be updated to accurately reflect the status of this account post-charge-off, or for the account to be deleted if FirstLight can not verify the accuracy of what they are reporting ; Written notice of the results of this investigation within 30 days as required by FCRA Section 1681i ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) ; If this account can not be verified as completely accurate, it must be deleted from my Experian credit report under FCRA Section 1681i ( a ) ( 5 ) ( A ).

Why this matters to me : Having this account reported the way it is makes my credit look worse than it should. The way the past-due date keeps updating makes lenders think this is a recent problem when it is actually from XXXX. That is hurting my ability to get credit, better interest rates, and other financial products I need. I am not trying to make a legitimate debt disappear I am asking for it to be reported in a way that is actually accurate and fair, which is what the law requires. 

I am also sending a copy of this letter and my credit report directly to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. They are a local credit union here in XXXX XXXX and I believe they may be willing to work with me to correct this if contacted directly. However, I want this formal complaint on record with the CFPB regardless.

If this is not resolved correctly, I am prepared to look into further options available to me under the FCRA, including FCRA Sections 1681n and 1681o, which allow consumers to seek damages for willful or negligent noncompliance by creditors or credit bureaus.

The collection account is allegedly associated with XXXX XXXX and is currently being reported as a collection account on my credit reports. 

I dispute the accuracy, validity, completeness, and continued reporting of this account. 

Most importantly, I possess written correspondence from the apartment complex confirming that no balance is owed. The original creditor has acknowledged that my account reflects a zero-dollar balance. 

Despite this written confirmation, Rent Recovery Solutions continues to furnish derogatory information regarding this account to consumer reporting agencies, causing ongoing damage to my credit profile and financial standing. 

Additionally, I previously filed a CFPB complaint concerning this matter. However, the complaint appears to have been closed without a meaningful investigation into the facts, without addressing the documentation provided, and without resolving the underlying dispute. 

To date, Rent Recovery Solutions has not provided competent evidence establishing that I owe the alleged debt. 

Furthermore, I never received any written notice from Rent Recovery Solutions regarding this alleged obligation. 

Prior to the appearance of this collection account on my credit reports, I did not receive : Any initial collection notice ; Any validation notice ; Any demand for payment ; Any account ledger ; Any itemized statement of charges ; Any move-out statement ; Any documentation identifying the basis of the alleged debt ; Any notice that Rent Recovery Solutions had been assigned, transferred, or otherwise obtained authority to collect the account. 

Instead, the account simply appeared on my credit report without warning in XXXX  and without any supporting documentation being provided to me. 

Because no collection notices were received and because the original creditor has confirmed that no balance is owed, I have serious concerns regarding the accuracy of the information being furnished by Rent Recovery Solutions. 

APPLICABLE FEDERAL LAW AND REGULATORY CONCERNS This matter raises significant concerns regarding compliance with the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( " FCRA '' ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.

The FCRA requires furnishers of information to provide accurate and complete information to consumer reporting agencies and to conduct reasonable investigations when consumers dispute information being reported. 

Specifically, I request an investigation into whether Rent Recovery Solutions has : Furnished inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading information ; Failed to conduct a reasonable investigation after receiving disputes regarding the account ; Continued reporting information that can not be substantiated ; Failed to correct or delete information that may be inaccurate ; Continued reporting a collection account despite evidence from the original creditor indicating that no balance is owed. 

The continued reporting of this account has adversely affected my creditworthiness and has caused ongoing financial harm. 

REQUESTED RESOLUTION I respectfully request that Rent Recovery Solutions provide competent evidence supporting the existence, validity, ownership, and amount of the alleged debt. 

Specifically, I request the following : XXXX. A complete account ledger showing how the alleged balance was calculated. 

XXXX. Copies of the lease agreement and any documents establishing liability. 

XXXX. Copies of move-out statements, final account statements, itemized charges, and payment records. 

XXXX. Documentation demonstrating that the alleged debt was assigned, transferred, or otherwise placed with Rent Recovery Solutions. 

XXXX. Documentation establishing Rent Recovery Solutions ' authority to collect and report the account. 

XXXX. Copies of all notices allegedly mailed to me concerning this debt. 

XXXX. Documentation showing the dates and addresses to which any notices were sent. 

XXXX. Documentation supporting the information currently furnished to Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. 

XXXX. Documentation showing that a reasonable investigation was conducted following my prior disputes and CFPB complaint. 

XXXX. Documentation establishing why the account continues to be reported despite written confirmation from the apartment complex that no balance is owed. 

Upon receipt and review of the requested documentation, I will evaluate the information and determine whether any legally enforceable balance exists. 

However, if Rent Recovery Solutions can not provide competent documentation substantiating the debt, validating the balance, and supporting its continued reporting, I request that the account be immediately removed from all consumer reporting agencies and that any inaccurate information previously furnished be corrected. 

I also request a written explanation of the findings of the investigation and copies of all supporting documentation relied upon in reaching those findings. 

I am attaching written correspondence from the apartment complex confirming that no balance is owed and request that this evidence be fully reviewed as part of the investigation. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

This is reinforced by the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, which strengthens requ

irements for accurate books and records and internal accounting controls sufficient to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the maintenance of accountability for assets.

Under the Bank Secrecy Act ( 31 U.S.C. 5311 et seq. ) and its implementing regulations, financial institutions must maintain customer account records, including statements, ledger cards, or other records showing each transaction in or with respect to customer accounts. These records must generally be retained for at least XXXX years and kept in a manner that makes them accessible in a reasonable period of time.
